steps_tex: Draw the head circle with the compass.
Draw the neck as a short vertical line below the circle.
Draw the body as a rectangle without the top edge: two vertical sides and a flat bottom.
Fix a radius and try the tip at different spots above the body until the arc from one top corner to the other touches the bottom of the neck line.
Draw the arc and rub out the trial marks.
item.answer_tex: Open ended. The head is a circle. The compass tip goes above the body (outside it, on the line through the middle of the body) at a point found by trial, and the radius is the distance from that tip to the top corners. The neck line joins the bottom of the head to the lowest point of the arc.

concept_name: The two properties of a rectangle and of a square

item.question: What shapes are a rectangle and four small squares drawn in a group? What makes them squares and rectangles?
steps: Look at a rectangle: its opposite sides are equal and each corner is a right angle.
Look at a square: all four sides are equal and each corner is a right angle.
item.answer: A rectangle has two properties: R1) its opposite sides are equal in length, and R2) all its angles are 90°. A square has: S1) all its sides are equal, and S2) all its angles are 90°.
item.text:

1. Look at a rectangle: its opposite sides are equal and each corner is a right angle.

Answer: A rectangle has two properties: R1) its opposite sides are equal in length, and R2) all its angles are 90°. A square has: S1) all its sides are equal, and S2) all its angles are 90°.

2. ABDC fails because B to D is a diagonal, not a side.
3. So go round the rectangle one corner after another.
Answer: No. ABDC and ACBD are not allowed. In a valid name the corners come in order, going round the rectangle, starting from any corner and going in either direction.

concept_name: A rotated square is still a square

item.question: A square piece of paper has all its sides equal and all angles 90°. It is rotated (tilted so it looks like a diamond). Is it still a square? Are all the sides still equal? Are all the angles still 90°?
steps: Rotating does not change lengths.
Rotating does not change angles.
So both square properties S1 and S2 still hold.
item.answer: Yes, it is still a square. All the sides are still equal and all the angles are still 90°, because rotating a square does not change its lengths and angles. In the same way a rotated rectangle is still a rectangle.
